title: Prove exact height-one integral shear biclique optimum six (no κ)
body:
## Summary

The height-one integral two-by-two matrix inventory has exact balanced rank-distance biclique optimum **six**. Twelve explicit commuting integral four-by-four shear frames attain K_(6,6), and a complete finite certificate excludes K_(7,7).

```text
S = {(-1,0),(-1,1),(0,-1),(0,1),(1,-1),(1,0)}
E(a,b) = [[a,b],[-a-b,a]]
O(a,b) = [[a,b],[b,-a-b]]
within-part difference rank = 2; cross-part difference rank = 1
```

Claim type: **exact finite certificate**, with a written construction and a proof reducing the upper bound to exhaustive computation. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. No new kappa or physical supplier is claimed.

This answers the first coefficient-height case of Open next question 2 in [petalas #6174](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6174), published October 29. That predecessor supplies an unbounded construction with quadratic-height upper bound; it does not give this exact bounded optimum. Credit CubeJerry #907 for the earlier eight-frame example and its abstract distortion theorem, eumemic #288 for the rational shear model, and navinor #825 / jeremydiviney #836 for the separate obstruction scopes. The cited distortion formula gives 5/3 on the new twelve-frame configuration. No predecessor scientific verifier is replayed.

Overlap refreshed before committing: all 768 cached open PR bodies and 7,363 Discussion records had complete remote pagination; the sparse local scan omitted 9,962 note paths. Separate distinctive-term searches covered main READMEs, merged PRs, live open biclique work and current claims. No matching height-one result was found; this is bounded overlap evidence, not proof of novelty.

Base main: `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19572817). TASK.json pins the full revision-8 `complex-rank-shape-decoder` card and records the changed scope as a coefficient-inventory side result. The contextual assessment is historical #5599, while the selected record is #7000 at kappa `363005817/100000000000`; that selected record is unchanged.

## Evidence

Before: the cited coefficient-height question had no height-one ceiling. After: the explicit six-by-six construction and two exhaustive upper checks agree.

- The determinant checker visits all 85,320 unordered triples among all 81 matrices and finds exactly 23,488 pairwise rank-two triples. Every one has at most six common rank-one contacts. The complete contact-count histogram is `{0:1480, 1:4368, 2:9624, 3:5760, 4:2096, 6:160}`.
- The separate checker imports no scientific code from the first. Exact Fraction elimination and all 61,236 first-row candidates recover the same histogram. It also checks all 144 ordered differences of the actual four-by-four shear frames.
- All four warning-strict normal/optimized VERIFY.json commands pass locally, each below one second against a 60-second limit. Ten rejecting controls, five elimination fixtures and both unexpected-argument controls pass. Generated receipts bind the witness, complete ordered triple trace and all seven package hashes.
- Registered replay and source metadata pass. At head `dadc7711829dfe8fbdcf663c466500395f5a0295`, all seven committed files, executable modes and full declared source ancestry pass. The official export passes integrity checks. All four commands also pass from a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH; every exported byte and mode is unchanged.

Local environment: CPython 3.12.15, Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, standard library only. Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/height-one-shear-bicliques/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/height-one-shear-bicliques/ceiling.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/height-one-shear-bicliques
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/height-one-shear-bicliques --check-source-history --check-modes
```

A CPython 3.12 executable at another path may replace the recorded interpreter. Expected direct markers are `PASS_HEIGHT_ONE_SHEAR_BICLIQUES` and `PASS_FIRST_ROW_SHEAR_CEILING`. The registered replay runs both verifiers in normal and optimized mode.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

Only integral two-by-two entries in {-1,0,1}, with rational ranks, are optimized. The result does not bound higher heights, bounded-denominator rational inventories, other dimensions or other fields. It gives no coding gain, legal native implementation, caller, dirty restoration, productive target bill, compiler closure or tape/precision implementation. The common-flag obstruction is not escaped by a non-L1 metric alone. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, complete multiplication theorem, independent human review or formal proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

## Open next questions

- Determine the balanced optimum at height two. First reduce the contact equations for its 625 matrices; a larger finite search or a general coefficient-height theorem remains missing.
- Supply a legal completed interface using the twelve frames, with explicit targets, arbitrary dirty inputs and paid cleanup, identifying a hypothesis beyond the known common-flag obstruction. No such realization or favorable complete bill is supplied here.

## Related open work

No open PR studying this bounded coefficient-height inventory was found in the live biclique/rank-metric searches and claim refresh. #6174 and #907 are merged predecessors. Other P104 subspace biclique packages study a different matrix inventory and do not compute a competing height-one optimum. The completion check read this account's seven other open PRs created since the CLAIM: #7469, #7471, #7472, #7473, #7474, #7476 and #7477. None studies this coefficient-height inventory or computes a competing optimum; no extra computations were run to check their results.

## CI notes

**CI did not certify this package.** At unchanged head `dadc7711829dfe8fbdcf663c466500395f5a0295`, [run 43289883200](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43289883200), [plan job 131432985031](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43289883200/job/131432985031), failed in `Onboarding helper tests` on exactly one of 760 tests, with 24 skipped:

```text
test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found
```

I read the completed checks once and inspected the actual job log. The package [replay job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43289883200/job/131436024807) was skipped because plan failed. No hosted mathematical or package verification is claimed.

I inspected main's own files at `e54523517`: `certificates/selected-result.json` requires `make frontier7000-verify`, while the current section of `docs/ci-verification.md` still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. The test at line 58 requires the selected command in that section. Neither those files nor the test is changed by this package.

I independently read the failed-job logs of [run 42905094314 / job 130140894651](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42905094314/job/130140894651), [run 42903313790 / job 130134720799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/42903313790/job/130134720799) and [run 43289715434 / job 131432409153](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43289715434/job/131432409153). All three show the same sole failing test, assertion, 760-test total and 24 skips. This is the existing repository-level navigation mismatch. The package's local normal/optimized, registered replay, source-history and read-only export checks passed as recorded above. No fix, retrigger commit, push or workflow rerun was made; maintainers own the repair of main.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: one isolated seven-file research package. Shared code, predecessor files, frozen evidence and the selected frontier are unchanged.
